title: ±inf in variance, correlation and Kahan sums
description: Any ±inf input makes `var_*`, `stddev_*` and `corr` NaN: the update computes `inf - inf`. `fsum` and `favg` of `[inf, 1]` are NaN, while `sum` and `avg` are `inf`.
One value: `var_samp` is NULL, `var_pop` 0, `corr(x, x)` NaN.
The docs are silent on NaN and infinity in every aggregate: a docs gap. No upstream test pins `fsum` and `favg` of `[inf, 1]`; it may change between versions.
`COVAR_*` follow the same rule: a NaN or ±inf on either side, or two equal infinities, make every moment NaN, without an error.

`nan_creation` of `sum` and `avg` of doubles (#341): `+inf` with `-inf` gives NaN, ungrouped, grouped and over a framed window; one kind of infinity with finite values gives that infinity; no error. A framed window sums each frame anew: a frame holding `-inf` and 1 after a frame that held `inf` and `-inf` is `-inf`, so no frame's NaN reaches the next. `fsum` and `favg` give NaN once a finite value follows an infinity, so their result depends on the order (`fsum` of 1, `inf` is `inf`, of `inf`, 1 NaN), and `favg` of one `inf` alone is NaN where `fsum` of it is `inf` (Kahan's error term `inf - inf`).
reference: `AggFn.var` and `AggFn.corr` of the same rows; the reference's handling of ±inf in these aggregates is part of #85. `nan_creation` is `ERROR` in the reference: a double `SUM` or `AVG` (grouped or over a window frame) of `+∞` and `-∞` is a domain error (D37, #257); `Profile.duckdb` has `NAN`, and #341 states DuckDB's NaN in the DuckDB lift.
